title: Bind research source reads to original Git objects
body:
## Summary

Local Git replacement refs can make the source readers return an original blob ID with a replacement's bytes. Scaffolding can then accept altered working bytes and record pins that fail in a clean checkout; an export can likewise contain replacement bytes under the original publication commit.

Set `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1` for the shared Git readers' subprocesses. Single reads, HEAD inventories, both batch protocols, scaffolding, metadata validation, publication-byte comparison and exports now read the stored objects. Six synthetic Git regressions cover blob and commit replacements, custom replacement namespaces, newline-path fallback, forged live pins and actual exported bytes/receipts. The parent environment and replacement refs are unchanged.

The registered `research/isolated-descendant-bytecode` consumer is also repaired: its helper row in `SOURCES.json` now says `provenance`, matching `verify.py`'s existing use of the authenticated historical Git blob. The original base, blob and SHA256 are retained. `VERIFY.json`, `TASK.json`, `verify.py`, `RESULT.json` and all three registered commands are unchanged. The current helper remains a declared replay input and the unchanged third command exercises its bytecode isolation. The README records the correction and preserves Arham Tahir's source credit; no validator exception or regenerated historical evidence is introduced.

Six source-role regressions cover the old failure versus corrected success, unchanged historical identities/evidence, corrupted blob/hash rejection, unrelated live-pin rejection, planner/publication coverage and deliberate live-isolation breakage rejected by the registered command. The same correction is included in both #3615 and #3635 so either can integrate first.

This is a `portable-replay` source/byte-binding repair, separate from the optional ancestry check. It does not establish mathematical correctness or a new selected result. Credit Nick Petalas's [PR3304](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3304) for the preceding immutable-object ancestry policy, Douglas Colkitt for the shared runner/scaffold, and Tekalign for the exporter.

## Validation

Local macOS arm64, CPython 3.12.14. Final tested commit: `05a7fa8434062016d733c3d92c0a4c4a53e52cc5`.

- [x] All six replacement regressions fail against the original reader: five assertion failures and one byte-mismatch error. The original implementation passed 67 focused tests and all six new methods under optimized Python with warnings treated as errors.
- [x] Final-head CI onboarding discovery: 277 tests, `OK (skipped=18)`; seven Linux `/proc` and 11 native Windows tests are inapplicable on this host.
- [x] Full affected registered consumer: unchanged 16-case historical differential, 11 isolated-runner tests and eight current-helper tests; `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.
- [x] Committed publication-byte/source-history preflight: 13 files; original source base `6f100d4bb5083f8c35d96fd95a539811c62f245c` retained.
- [x] Combined #3615 and #3635 production changes: all 15 new regression methods and the full affected registered replay pass.
- [x] `git diff --check`.
- [ ] Hosted CI and native Windows/Linux execution. No repository-wide historical/theorem replay or selected-frontier cold replay is claimed.

```sh
python3.12 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py' -v
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/isolated-descendant-bytecode
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/isolated-descendant-bytecode --check-source-history
git diff --check
```

Canonical main was rechecked unchanged at `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6. The refreshed overlap inventory includes 344 open PRs, 2,964 closed PRs and 2,453 Discussion records, with complete pagination and no warnings. PR3304 left the shared readers unchanged; no equivalent correction was identified. This is not an exhaustive novelty claim.

Prepared for roger-sato with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in diagnosis, implementation, regression tests and writing. Apache-2.0. Same-session agent review is not independent human acceptance.
